sections.html: Asia: Myanmar; reported from Thailand. Type locality: Irrawaddy, Bassein district, and Salween in the Tenasserim provinces, Burma. The species also occurs in India and Bangladesh. It is known from the lower reaches and estuaries of the Irrawaddy and Salween drainages eastwards to the western part of the Malay Peninsula.
Freshwater; brackish; benthopelagic; amphidromous. Found in freshwaters and tidal rivers.

The specific name burmanicus means Burmese, referring to the type locality at Salween, Burma (now Myanmar). It is still found on some online searches listed as Cochlefelis burmanicus.

IUCN Red List: assessed as Least Concern given its presence in a number of river basins and the absence of known threats, although information on the species' range, distribution and threats is lacking. The species should be reassessed if further information becomes available on the likely or actual impact of hydropower dams on the Irrawaddy and Salween rivers (IUCN 2010).
